:::{#rem-symmetric-in-statistics}
#### Symmetric matrices in statistics

Covariance matrices are symmetric:
entry $(i, j)$ of the covariance matrix of a random vector $\vecf{Y}$
is $\Cov{Y_i, Y_j}$,
and $\Cov{Y_i, Y_j} = \Cov{Y_j, Y_i}$.
For example, if $\Var{Y_1} = 4$, $\Var{Y_2} = 9$, and $\Cov{Y_1, Y_2} = 1$,
the covariance matrix of $(Y_1, Y_2)$ is

$$
\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 9 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Fisher information matrices are symmetric for the same reason:
the Fisher information is the covariance matrix of the score.

:::
